Overview

The boolean search feature provides a powerful query language for finding entities using logical expressions. Instead of simple keyword matching, you can construct complex queries with AND, OR, NOT operators, field-specific searches, and exact phrase matching.

Key Features

✅ 

Logical Operators

: AND, OR, NOT for combining search terms

✅ 

Parentheses

: Group expressions for complex logic

✅ 

Field-Specific

: Search in specific fields (name, type, observation, tag)

✅ 

Quoted Strings

: Exact phrase matching

✅ 

Case-Insensitive

: All searches ignore case

✅ 

Recursive Parser

: Handles deeply nested expressions

When to Use Boolean Search

Use Case

Tool

Example

Simple keyword

search_nodes

Find entities with "project"

Typo-tolerant

fuzzy_search

Find "projct" → "project"

Relevance ranking

search_nodes_ranked

Best matches for "machine learning"

Complex logic

boolean_search

"project AND (frontend OR backend) NOT deprecated"


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Basic Syntax

Simple Terms

Search for a single term:

project


Matches:

 Any entity with "project" in name, type, observations, or tags

Multiple Terms (Implicit AND)

Space-separated terms are implicitly joined with AND:

machine learning


Equivalent to:

 

machine AND learning

Matches:

 Entities containing BOTH "machine" AND "learning"

Case Insensitivity

All searches are case-insensitive:

PROJECT = project = Project = PrOjEcT



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Logical Operators

AND Operator

Requires BOTH terms to match:

frontend AND react


Matches:

✅ "React Frontend Project"

✅ Entity with observations: ["Frontend development", "Using React"]

❌ "Frontend Vue Project" (no "react")

❌ "React Native Mobile" (no "frontend")

Syntax:

term1 AND term2
term1 && term2      (NOT supported)
term1 term2         (implicit AND)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


OR Operator

Requires AT LEAST ONE term to match:

frontend OR backend


Matches:

✅ "Frontend Development"

✅ "Backend API"

✅ "Full Stack Frontend and Backend" (both)

❌ "Mobile Application" (neither)

Syntax:

term1 OR term2
term1 || term2      (NOT supported)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


NOT Operator

Excludes entities matching the term:

project NOT deprecated


Matches:

✅ "Active Project"

✅ "New Project Alpha"

❌ "Deprecated Project" (contains "deprecated")

❌ "Old Deprecated System" (contains "deprecated")

Syntax:

NOT term
!term               (NOT supported)
-term               (NOT supported)


Important:

 NOT must be followed by a term or expression:

✅ NOT deprecated
✅ NOT (old OR obsolete)
❌ project AND NOT       (invalid - nothing after NOT)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Field-Specific Search

Syntax

Search in specific fields using 

field:term

 syntax:

name:project
type:task
observation:"bug fix"
tag:urgent


Available fields:

name:

 - Entity name only

type:

 - Entity type only

observation:

 - Observations only

tag:

 - Tags only

Examples

Search by Name

name:alpha


Matches:

✅ Name: "Project Alpha"

✅ Name: "Alpha Version"

❌ Name: "Project Beta", Observation: "Alpha release" (not in name)

Search by Type

type:project


Matches:

 All entities with 

entityType === "project"

Search by Observation

observation:bug


Matches:

 Entities with "bug" in ANY observation

Search by Tag

tag:urgent


Matches:

 Entities with "urgent" tag

Combining Field Searches

type:project AND tag:urgent


Matches:

 Urgent projects only

name:api OR type:api


Matches:

 Entities with "api" in name OR type "api"

observation:"bug fix" AND NOT tag:completed


Matches:

 Bug fix observations that aren't completed


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Quoted Strings

Exact Phrase Matching

Use quotes for exact multi-word phrases:

"machine learning"


Matches:

✅ "Machine Learning Project"

✅ Observation: "Uses machine learning algorithms"

❌ "Machine intelligence and deep learning" (not exact phrase)

With Field Specifiers

observation:"bug fix"


Matches:

 Observations containing exact phrase "bug fix"

name:"Project Alpha"


Matches:

 Entities with exact name "Project Alpha"

Escaping Quotes

To include quotes within quoted strings, escape with backslash:

"The \"Best\" Project"


Matches:

 Entities containing 

The "Best" Project


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Operator Precedence

Operators are evaluated in this order (highest to lowest):

Parentheses

 

( )

NOT

AND

OR

Examples

A AND B OR C


Evaluated as:

 

(A AND B) OR C

Matches:

 (A and B) or C


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


A OR B AND C


Evaluated as:

 

A OR (B AND C)

Matches:

 A or (B and C)


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


NOT A AND B


Evaluated as:

 

(NOT A) AND B

Matches:

 Not A, but B


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Using Parentheses

Override precedence with parentheses:

(A OR B) AND C


Matches:

 (A or B) and C

NOT (A OR B)


Matches:

 Neither A nor B

(frontend OR backend) AND (react OR vue) NOT deprecated


Evaluated as:

 

((frontend OR backend) AND (react OR vue)) AND (NOT deprecated)

Matches:

 Entities that are:

(Frontend OR Backend) AND

(React OR Vue) AND

NOT Deprecated


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Query Examples

Example 1: Find Active Projects

type:project NOT tag:completed NOT tag:deprecated


Finds:

 Projects that are not completed or deprecated


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 2: Find Frontend or Backend Tasks

type:task AND (observation:frontend OR observation:backend)


Finds:

 Tasks mentioning frontend or backend in observations


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 3: Find Urgent or High Priority

tag:urgent OR tag:high-priority


Finds:

 Entities tagged as urgent or high-priority


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 4: Find API Documentation

name:api AND type:document


Finds:

 Documents with "api" in the name


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 5: Find Bug Fixes Not Completed

observation:"bug fix" NOT tag:completed


Finds:

 Entities with bug fix observations that aren't completed


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 6: Complex Project Search

type:project AND (tag:frontend OR tag:backend) AND NOT (tag:deprecated OR tag:on-hold)


Finds:

 Projects that are:

Type "project" AND

Tagged as frontend OR backend AND

NOT deprecated AND NOT on-hold


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 7: Find React or Vue Projects

(name:react OR observation:react OR tag:react) AND type:project
OR
(name:vue OR observation:vue OR tag:vue) AND type:project


Finds:

 Projects mentioning React or Vue in any field


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Example 8: Exclude Test Data

machine learning NOT (tag:test OR tag:draft OR name:test)


Finds:

 Machine learning entities that aren't test/draft data


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Common Patterns

Pattern 1: Technology Stack Search

Find entities using specific technologies:

(react OR vue OR angular) AND (typescript OR javascript)


Use Case:

 Find frontend projects using modern frameworks


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 2: Status Filtering

Find entities in specific states:

type:task AND tag:in-progress NOT tag:blocked


Use Case:

 Find active, unblocked tasks


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 3: Priority Filtering

Find high-priority work:

(tag:urgent OR tag:high-priority) AND NOT tag:completed


Use Case:

 Focus on important incomplete work


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 4: Multi-Domain Search

Search across multiple domains:

(type:project OR type:feature OR type:epic) AND observation:authentication


Use Case:

 Find all work items related to authentication


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 5: Exclusion Search

Find entities NOT matching criteria:

type:project NOT (tag:archived OR tag:deprecated OR tag:on-hold)


Use Case:

 Find only active projects


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 6: Exact Name Matching

Find entities with exact names:

name:"Project Alpha" OR name:"Project Beta"


Use Case:

 Find specific named entities


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 7: Composite Field Search

Search across multiple fields for same term:

api AND (name:api OR type:api OR observation:api)


Simplified:

 Just use 

api

 (searches all fields by default)

Use when:

 You need explicit field matching


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 8: Tag Combination Search

Find entities with specific tag combinations:

tag:frontend AND tag:react AND NOT tag:legacy


Use Case:

 Find modern frontend React projects


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Best Practices

1. Start Simple, Add Complexity

Build queries incrementally:

# Step 1: Basic search
project

# Step 2: Add type filter
type:project

# Step 3: Add status filter
type:project NOT tag:completed

# Step 4: Add priority filter
type:project NOT tag:completed AND (tag:urgent OR tag:high-priority)


2. Use Parentheses for Clarity

Even when not required, parentheses improve readability:

❌ Hard to read:
A AND B OR C AND D NOT E

✅ Clear:
(A AND B) OR (C AND D AND NOT E)


3. Field-Specific When Possible

Be specific to improve precision:

❌ Broad:
api

✅ Precise:
name:api OR type:api

✅ Very precise:
type:api AND tag:rest


4. Combine with Other Search Tools

Use the right tool for the job:

// Simple search: use search_nodes
await search_nodes({ query: "project" })

// Typo-tolerant: use fuzzy_search
await fuzzy_search({ query: "projct", threshold: 0.8 })

// Ranked results: use search_nodes_ranked
await search_nodes_ranked({ query: "machine learning", limit: 10 })

// Complex logic: use boolean_search
await boolean_search({ query: "type:project AND (frontend OR backend) NOT deprecated" })


javascript

5. Test Queries Incrementally

Verify each part of complex queries:

// Test parts separately
await boolean_search({ query: "frontend OR backend" })
await boolean_search({ query: "type:project" })
await boolean_search({ query: "NOT deprecated" })

// Combine after verification
await boolean_search({
  query: "type:project AND (frontend OR backend) NOT deprecated"
})


javascript

6. Save Complex Queries

Use saved searches for frequently used queries:

// Save complex query
await save_search({
  name: "Active Frontend Projects",
  query: "type:project AND tag:frontend NOT (tag:completed OR tag:deprecated)",
  description: "All active frontend projects"
})

// Execute later
await execute_saved_search({ name: "Active Frontend Projects" })


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Troubleshooting

Issue: No Results Found

Problem:

 Query returns empty results

Solutions:

Simplify query

 - Remove operators one by one:

// Original (no results)
boolean_search({ query: "type:project AND frontend AND react NOT deprecated" })

// Simplify
boolean_search({ query: "type:project" })  // Does this work?
boolean_search({ query: "frontend" })       // Does this work?


javascript

Check field names

 - Ensure field specifiers are correct:

❌ boolean_search({ query: "entityType:project" })  // Wrong field name
✅ boolean_search({ query: "type:project" })        // Correct


javascript

Check spelling

 - Use fuzzy search first:

await fuzzy_search({ query: "fronted" })  // Suggests "frontend"


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Issue: Too Many Results

Problem:

 Query is too broad

Solutions:

Add more constraints

:

// Too broad
boolean_search({ query: "project" })

// More specific
boolean_search({ query: "type:project AND tag:active" })

// Very specific
boolean_search({
  query: "type:project AND tag:active AND NOT tag:on-hold AND observation:react"
})


javascript

Use field-specific searches

:

// Searches all fields (broad)
boolean_search({ query: "api" })

// Only in name (narrow)
boolean_search({ query: "name:api" })


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Issue: Syntax Error

Problem:

 Query parser fails

Common causes:

Unclosed quotes

:

❌ boolean_search({ query: "machine learning" })  // Missing closing quote
✅ boolean_search({ query: "\"machine learning\"" })


javascript

Invalid field names

:

❌ boolean_search({ query: "title:project" })    // No "title" field
✅ boolean_search({ query: "name:project" })


javascript

Dangling operators

:

❌ boolean_search({ query: "project AND" })      // Nothing after AND
✅ boolean_search({ query: "project AND task" })


javascript

Mismatched parentheses

:

❌ boolean_search({ query: "(frontend OR backend" })  // Missing )
✅ boolean_search({ query: "(frontend OR backend)" })


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Issue: Unexpected Results

Problem:

 Results don't match expectations

Debug steps:

Check operator precedence

:

// Query: A OR B AND C
// Evaluated as: A OR (B AND C)
// NOT as: (A OR B) AND C

// Use parentheses to control:
boolean_search({ query: "(A OR B) AND C" })


javascript

Verify field matching

:

// Get entity details
const results = await boolean_search({ query: "your query" })
const details = await open_nodes({ names: results.map(e => e.name) })
console.log(details)  // Check why each entity matched


javascript

Test with simple queries

:

// Does the entity match this?
await boolean_search({ query: "frontend" })

// Does it match this?
await boolean_search({ query: "type:project" })

// Why doesn't it match the combination?
await boolean_search({ query: "type:project AND frontend" })


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Issue: Query is Slow

Problem:

 Complex query takes too long

Solutions:

Simplify query

 - Reduce complexity:

// Complex (slow)
boolean_search({
  query: "(A OR B OR C OR D) AND (E OR F OR G OR H) AND NOT (I OR J OR K)"
})

// Simplified (faster)
boolean_search({ query: "(A OR B) AND E NOT I" })


javascript

Use other search tools

 - Boolean search evaluates every entity:

// If you just need keyword matching, use search_nodes
await search_nodes({ query: "project" })

// If you need ranking, use search_nodes_ranked
await search_nodes_ranked({ query: "machine learning" })


javascript

Filter before searching

 - Combine with other filters:

// Filter by tags first, then boolean search
const tagged = await search_nodes({ query: "", tags: ["active"] })
// Then manually apply boolean logic to this smaller set


javascript

Integration Examples

With Saved Searches

// Save complex boolean query
await save_search({
  name: "Active Backend APIs",
  query: "type:api AND tag:backend AND NOT (tag:deprecated OR tag:draft)",
  description: "Production backend APIs only"

// Execute saved search

  name: "Active Backend APIs"

console.log(`Found ${results.length} active backend APIs`)


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


With Tags

// Find entities to tag
const results = await boolean_search({
  query: "type:project AND observation:\"machine learning\" NOT tag:ml"
})

// Tag them
await add_tags_to_multiple({
  entityNames: results.map(e => e.name),
  tags: ["ml", "machine-learning"]
})

console.log(`Tagged ${results.length} machine learning projects`)


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


With Hierarchies

// Find projects with active children
const projects = await boolean_search({
  query: "type:project NOT tag:completed"
})

for (const project of projects) {
  const children = await get_children({ entityName: project.name })

  const activeChildren = children.filter(child =>
    !child.tags?.includes("completed")
  )

  if (activeChildren.length > 0) {
    console.log(`${project.name}: ${activeChildren.length} active children`)
  }
}


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


With Export

// Export search results
const results = await boolean_search({
  query: "type:project AND tag:2025-q1 NOT tag:cancelled"
})

// Export just these entities
const entityNames = results.map(e => e.name)
const subtrees = await Promise.all(
  entityNames.map(name => get_subtree({ entityName: name }))
)

// Combine and export
// (Export logic depends on your needs)


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Advanced Query Patterns

Pattern 1: Multi-Condition OR

Find entities matching ANY of several complete conditions:

(type:project AND tag:urgent)
OR
(type:task AND tag:high-priority)
OR
(type:bug AND tag:critical)


Use Case:

 Find all high-priority work across different types


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 2: Nested Exclusions

Complex exclusion logic:

type:project NOT (
  tag:completed OR
  tag:cancelled OR
  (tag:on-hold AND NOT tag:urgent)
)


Use Case:

 Find active projects, including urgent ones on hold


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 3: Field Combination Matrix

Search multiple terms across multiple fields:

(name:api OR type:api OR observation:api OR tag:api)
AND
(name:rest OR observation:rest OR tag:rest)


Use Case:

 Find REST APIs mentioned anywhere


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Pattern 4: Temporal + Status

Combine with other search filters:

// Boolean search for type
const results = await boolean_search({
  query: "type:project AND tag:active"
})

// Further filter by date
const sixMonthsAgo = new Date()
sixMonthsAgo.setMonth(sixMonthsAgo.getMonth() - 6)

const recentActive = results.filter(e => {
  const lastModified = new Date(e.lastModified || e.createdAt)
  return lastModified > sixMonthsAgo
})

console.log(`${recentActive.length} recently active projects`)


javascript


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Summary

Boolean search provides powerful query capabilities:

✅ 

Logical Operators

: AND, OR, NOT for complex logic

 

✅ 

Field-Specific

: Search name, type, observation, tag fields

 

✅ 

Quoted Strings

: Exact phrase matching

 

✅ 

Parentheses

: Group expressions for precedence control

 

✅ 

Case-Insensitive

: Flexible matching

 

✅ 

Recursive Parser

: Handle deeply nested queries

Query Template:

[field:]term [AND|OR] [field:]term [NOT] [field:]term


Operator Precedence:

Parentheses 

( )

NOT

AND

OR

Best Practices:

Start simple, add complexity incrementally

Use parentheses for clarity

Be field-specific when possible

Test queries incrementally

Save complex queries for reuse

Combine with other search tools

 for organizing entities

 for duplicate detection

## docs\guides\TASKSCHEDULER_INTEGRATION.md



TaskScheduler Integration Guide

Phase 9B

: This guide documents how to integrate the TaskScheduler's progress tracking and cancellation support with long-running operations in the Memory MCP server.

Overview

Phase 9B introduces unified progress tracking and cancellation support across all long-running operations in the Memory MCP server. This enables:

Progress Reporting

: Real-time feedback on operation progress (0-100%)

Cancellation

: Ability to abort long-running operations via 

AbortSignal

Consistent API

: All operations use the same 

LongRunningOperationOptions

 interface

Core Types

LongRunningOperationOptions

The standard interface for all long-running operations:

interface LongRunningOperationOptions {
  /** Progress callback for tracking operation progress */
  onProgress?: ProgressCallback;

  /** AbortSignal for cancellation support */
  signal?: AbortSignal;

  /** Priority for queued operations (optional) */
  priority?: TaskPriority;
}


typescript

ProgressCallback

The callback signature for progress updates:

type ProgressCallback = (progress: {
  completed: number;
  total: number;
  percentage: number;
  currentTaskId?: string;
}) => void;


typescript

OperationCancelledError

Thrown when an operation is cancelled:

class OperationCancelledError extends KnowledgeGraphError {
  constructor(operation?: string);
}


typescript

Supported Operations

EntityManager

// Create entities with progress tracking
const entities = await entityManager.createEntities(entityArray, {
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

CompressionManager

// Find duplicates with progress tracking
const duplicates = await compressionManager.findDuplicates(0.8, {
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});

// Compress graph with progress tracking
const result = await compressionManager.compressGraph(0.8, false, {
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

IOManager

// Import graph with progress tracking
const result = await ioManager.importGraph('json', data, 'merge', false, {
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

ArchiveManager

// Archive entities with progress tracking
const result = await archiveManager.archiveEntities(criteria, {
  dryRun: false,
  saveToFile: true,
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

SemanticSearch

// Index all entities with cancellation support
const result = await semanticSearch.indexAll(graph, {
  forceReindex: false,
  onProgress: (current, total) => console.log(`${current}/${total}`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

TransactionManager

// Commit transaction with progress tracking
txManager.begin();
txManager.createEntity({ name: 'Alice', entityType: 'person', observations: [] });
const result = await txManager.commit({
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

GraphTraversal

// Find all paths with cancellation support
const paths = await graphTraversal.findAllPaths('source', 'target', 5, {
  direction: 'both',
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

StreamingExporter

// Stream export with progress tracking
const exporter = new StreamingExporter('/path/to/output.jsonl');
const result = await exporter.streamJSONL(graph, {
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.percentage}% complete`),
  signal: controller.signal,
});


typescript

Utility Functions

checkCancellation

Checks if an operation has been cancelled and throws 

OperationCancelledError

:

import { checkCancellation } from '../utils/index.js';

async function myLongRunningOperation(options?: LongRunningOperationOptions) {
  // Check at start
  checkCancellation(options?.signal, 'myOperation');

  for (const item of items) {
    // Check periodically during processing
    checkCancellation(options?.signal, 'myOperation');
    await processItem(item);
  }
}


typescript

createProgressReporter

Creates a throttled progress reporter to avoid excessive callbacks:

import { createProgressReporter, createProgress } from '../utils/index.js';

async function myOperation(options?: LongRunningOperationOptions) {
  const reportProgress = createProgressReporter(options?.onProgress);
  const total = items.length;

  reportProgress?.(createProgress(0, total, 'myOperation'));

  for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
    await processItem(items[i]);
    reportProgress?.(createProgress(i + 1, total, 'myOperation'));
  }
}


typescript

executeWithPhases

Executes an operation with multiple distinct phases:

import { executeWithPhases } from '../utils/index.js';

const results = await executeWithPhases([
  { name: 'parsing', weight: 20, execute: async () => parseData() },
  { name: 'processing', weight: 60, execute: async () => processEntities() },
  { name: 'saving', weight: 20, execute: async () => saveResults() },
], options?.onProgress, options?.signal);


typescript

processBatchesWithProgress

Processes items in batches with automatic progress tracking:

import { processBatchesWithProgress } from '../utils/index.js';

const results = await processBatchesWithProgress(
  items,
  100, // batch size
  async (batch) => {
    for (const item of batch) {
      await saveItem(item);
    }
    return batch.length;
  },
  options?.onProgress,
  options?.signal,
  'batchOperation'
);


typescript

Implementation Pattern

When implementing progress tracking in a new operation:

Import utilities

:

import type { LongRunningOperationOptions } from '../types/index.js';
import { checkCancellation, createProgressReporter, createProgress } from '../utils/index.js';


typescript

Add options parameter

:

async myMethod(data: MyData, options?: LongRunningOperationOptions): Promise<Result> {


typescript

Check for early cancellation

:

checkCancellation(options?.signal, 'myMethod');


typescript

Setup progress reporter

:

const reportProgress = createProgressReporter(options?.onProgress);
reportProgress?.(createProgress(0, total, 'myMethod'));


typescript

Report progress during processing

:

for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
  checkCancellation(options?.signal, 'myMethod');
  await processItem(items[i]);
  reportProgress?.(createProgress(i + 1, total, 'myMethod'));
}


typescript

Report completion

:

reportProgress?.(createProgress(total, total, 'myMethod'));
return result;


typescript

Handling Cancellation

Operations should handle cancellation gracefully:

try {
  await longRunningOperation({ signal: controller.signal });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof OperationCancelledError) {
    console.log('Operation was cancelled');
    // Perform cleanup if needed
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}


typescript

Best Practices

Check cancellation at natural breakpoints

 - Don't check on every iteration if the loop body is fast

Report progress at meaningful intervals

 - Use throttling to avoid overwhelming the callback

Use phase-based progress for multi-step operations

 - Helps users understand which step is running

Clean up resources on cancellation

 - Close files, rollback transactions, etc.

Document cancellation behavior

 - Specify what state the system is in after cancellation

Test cancellation paths

 - Ensure cancellation at various points works correctly

Error Handling

All operations that support cancellation will throw 

OperationCancelledError

 when cancelled:

import { OperationCancelledError } from '../utils/errors.js';

try {
  await myOperation({ signal: controller.signal });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof OperationCancelledError) {
    // Handle cancellation
    console.log(`Operation '${error.message}' was cancelled`);
  }
}

Transaction Batching API

 - Estimate and optimize query cost before execution

\n * Internal structure for tracking pending operations in a batch transaction.\n * @internal\n */\ninterface PendingOperations {\n  entitiesToCreate: EntityInput[];\n  entitiesToUpdate: { name: string; updates: Partial

 }[];\n  entitiesToDelete: Set

;\n  relationsToCreate: RelationInput[];\n  relationsToDelete: { from: string; to: string; relationType: string }[];\n  observationsToAdd: ObservationInput[];\n  tagsToAdd: { entityName: string; tags: string[] }[];\n  importanceToSet: { entityName: string; importance: number }[];\n}"

"step": 5,

"action": "Add the BatchTransaction class",

"code": "/

\n * Collects multiple operations for atomic batch execution.\n *\n * This class implements BatchTransactionContext and is used internally\n * by GraphStorage.transaction() to collect operations before executing\n * them in a single lock/save cycle.\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * // Used internally by GraphStorage.transaction():\n * const tx = new BatchTransaction();\n * tx.createEntities([...]);\n * tx.createRelations([...]);\n * const pending = tx.getPendingOperations();\n * // Execute all pending operations atomically\n * 

\n */\nexport class BatchTransaction implements BatchTransactionContext {\n  private pending: PendingOperations = {\n    entitiesToCreate: [],\n    entitiesToUpdate: [],\n    entitiesToDelete: new Set(),\n    relationsToCreate: [],\n    relationsToDelete: [],\n    observationsToAdd: [],\n    tagsToAdd: [],\n    importanceToSet: [],\n  };\n\n  createEntities(entities: EntityInput[]): void {\n    this.pending.entitiesToCreate.push(...entities);\n  }\n\n  createRelations(relations: RelationInput[]): void {\n    this.pending.relationsToCreate.push(...relations);\n  }\n\n  addObservations(observations: ObservationInput[]): void {\n    this.pending.observationsToAdd.push(...observations);\n  }\n\n  deleteEntities(entityNames: string[]): void {\n    for (const name of entityNames) {\n      this.pending.entitiesToDelete.add(name);\n    }\n  }\n\n  deleteRelations(relations: { from: string; to: string; relationType: string }[]): void {\n    this.pending.relationsToDelete.push(...relations);\n  }\n\n  updateEntities(updates: { name: string; updates: Partial

<Entity>

 }[]): void {\n    this.pending.entitiesToUpdate.push(...updates);\n  }\n\n  addTags(entityName: string, tags: string[]): void {\n    this.pending.tagsToAdd.push({ entityName, tags });\n  }\n\n  setImportance(entityName: string, importance: number): void {\n    this.pending.importanceToSet.push({ entityName, importance });\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get the pending operations for execution.\n   * @internal Used by GraphStorage.transaction() to apply operations.\n   */\n  getPendingOperations(): PendingOperations {\n    return this.pending;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Check if any operations are pending.\n   */\n  hasPendingOperations(): boolean {\n    return (\n      this.pending.entitiesToCreate.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.entitiesToUpdate.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.entitiesToDelete.size > 0 ||\n      this.pending.relationsToCreate.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.relationsToDelete.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.observationsToAdd.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.tagsToAdd.length > 0 ||\n      this.pending.importanceToSet.length > 0\n    );\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get statistics about pending operations.\n   */\n  getStats(): {\n    entities: { create: number; update: number; delete: number };\n    relations: { create: number; delete: number };\n    observations: number;\n    tags: number;\n    importance: number;\n  } {\n    return {\n      entities: {\n        create: this.pending.entitiesToCreate.length,\n        update: this.pending.entitiesToUpdate.length,\n        delete: this.pending.entitiesToDelete.size,\n      },\n      relations: {\n        create: this.pending.relationsToCreate.length,\n        delete: this.pending.relationsToDelete.length,\n      },\n      observations: this.pending.observationsToAdd.length,\n      tags: this.pending.tagsToAdd.length,\n      importance: this.pending.importanceToSet.length,\n    };\n  }\n}"

},

"code": "/

\n * Execute multiple operations in a single atomic transaction.\n *\n * All operations share a single lock/unlock cycle and single save operation,\n * making batch operations 2-10x faster than individual calls.\n *\n * Operations are applied in this order:\n * 1. Create entities\n * 2. Create relations\n * 3. Add observations\n * 4. Add tags\n * 5. Set importance\n * 6. Update entities\n * 7. Delete entities (and their relations)\n * 8. Delete specific relations\n *\n * @param callback - Function that receives BatchTransactionContext and queues operations\n * @returns Transaction result with statistics\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * const result = await storage.transaction((tx) => {\n *   tx.createEntities([\n *     { name: 'Alice', entityType: 'person', observations: ['Engineer'] },\n *     { name: 'Bob', entityType: 'person', observations: ['Designer'] },\n *   ]);\n *   tx.createRelations([\n *     { from: 'Alice', to: 'Bob', relationType: 'knows' },\n *   ]);\n *   tx.addTags('Alice', ['tech', 'senior']);\n *   tx.setImportance('Bob', 8);\n * });\n * console.log(`Created ${result.entitiesCreated} entities in ${result.durationMs}ms`);\n * 

\n */\nasync transaction(\n  callback: (tx: BatchTransactionContext) => void | Promise

<void>

\n): Promise

<BatchTransactionResult>

 {\n  const startTime = Date.now();\n  const tx = new BatchTransaction();\n\n  // Execute callback to collect operations\n  await callback(tx);\n\n  // Early return if no operations queued\n  if (!tx.hasPendingOperations()) {\n    return {\n      success: true,\n      entitiesCreated: 0,\n      entitiesUpdated: 0,\n      entitiesDeleted: 0,\n      relationsCreated: 0,\n      relationsDeleted: 0,\n      observationsAdded: 0,\n      durationMs: Date.now() - startTime,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Acquire lock once for all operations\n  const release = await this.mutex.acquire();\n  try {\n    await this.ensureLoaded();\n    const graph = await this.getGraphForMutation();\n    const pending = tx.getPendingOperations();\n    const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();\n\n    let entitiesCreated = 0;\n    let entitiesUpdated = 0;\n    let entitiesDeleted = 0;\n    let relationsCreated = 0;\n    let relationsDeleted = 0;\n    let observationsAdded = 0;\n\n    // Build entity lookup map\n    const entityMap = new Map(graph.entities.map(e => [e.name, e]));\n\n    // 1. Create entities\n    for (const input of pending.entitiesToCreate) {\n      if (!entityMap.has(input.name)) {\n        const entity: Entity = {\n          name: input.name,\n          entityType: input.entityType,\n          observations: [...input.observations],\n          tags: input.tags?.map(t => t.toLowerCase()),\n          importance: input.importance,\n          parentId: input.parentId,\n          createdAt: timestamp,\n          lastModified: timestamp,\n        };\n        graph.entities.push(entity);\n        entityMap.set(entity.name, entity);\n        entitiesCreated++;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 2. Create relations\n    for (const input of pending.relationsToCreate) {\n      const exists = graph.relations.some(\n        r => r.from === input.from && r.to === input.to && r.relationType === input.relationType\n      );\n      if (!exists) {\n        graph.relations.push({\n          from: input.from,\n          to: input.to,\n          relationType: input.relationType,\n          createdAt: timestamp,\n          lastModified: timestamp,\n        });\n        relationsCreated++;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 3. Add observations\n    for (const { entityName, contents } of pending.observationsToAdd) {\n      const entity = entityMap.get(entityName);\n      if (entity) {\n        entity.observations.push(...contents);\n        entity.lastModified = timestamp;\n        observationsAdded += contents.length;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 4. Add tags\n    for (const { entityName, tags } of pending.tagsToAdd) {\n      const entity = entityMap.get(entityName);\n      if (entity) {\n        const normalizedTags = tags.map(t => t.toLowerCase());\n        entity.tags = [...new Set([...(entity.tags ?? []), ...normalizedTags])];\n        entity.lastModified = timestamp;\n        entitiesUpdated++;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 5. Set importance\n    for (const { entityName, importance } of pending.importanceToSet) {\n      const entity = entityMap.get(entityName);\n      if (entity) {\n        entity.importance = importance;\n        entity.lastModified = timestamp;\n        entitiesUpdated++;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 6. Update entities\n    for (const { name, updates } of pending.entitiesToUpdate) {\n      const entity = entityMap.get(name);\n      if (entity) {\n        Object.assign(entity, updates);\n        entity.lastModified = timestamp;\n        entitiesUpdated++;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // 7. Delete entities (and cascade delete their relations)\n    if (pending.entitiesToDelete.size > 0) {\n      const originalCount = graph.entities.length;\n      graph.entities = graph.entities.filter(e => !pending.entitiesToDelete.has(e.name));\n      entitiesDeleted = originalCount - graph.entities.length;\n\n      // Cascade delete relations involving deleted entities\n      graph.relations = graph.relations.filter(\n        r => !pending.entitiesToDelete.has(r.from) && !pending.entitiesToDelete.has(r.to)\n      );\n    }\n\n    // 8. Delete specific relations\n    if (pending.relationsToDelete.length > 0) {\n      const toDelete = new Set(\n        pending.relationsToDelete.map(r => 

${r.from}|${r.to}|${r.relationType}

)\n      );\n      const originalCount = graph.relations.length;\n      graph.relations = graph.relations.filter(\n        r => !toDelete.has(

${r.from}|${r.to}|${r.relationType}

)\n      );\n      relationsDeleted = originalCount - graph.relations.length;\n    }\n\n    // Single save for all operations\n    await this.saveGraph(graph);\n\n    return {\n      success: true,\n      entitiesCreated,\n      entitiesUpdated,\n      entitiesDeleted,\n      relationsCreated,\n      relationsDeleted,\n      observationsAdded,\n      durationMs: Date.now() - startTime,\n    };\n  } finally {\n    release();\n  }\n}"

\n * Graph Event Emitter\n *\n * Type-safe EventEmitter for graph change notifications.\n * Enables real-time sync, audit logging, and cache invalidation.\n *\n * @module core/GraphEventEmitter\n */\n\nimport { EventEmitter } from 'events';\nimport type { Entity, Relation } from '../types/types.js';\n\n/

\n * Event types emitted by the graph.\n */\nexport type GraphEventType =\n  | 'entityCreated'\n  | 'entityUpdated'\n  | 'entityDeleted'\n  | 'relationCreated'\n  | 'relationDeleted'\n  | 'observationAdded'\n  | 'observationDeleted'\n  | 'graphLoaded'\n  | 'graphSaved';"

 

},

/\n  changes: Partial

;\n  /

* Previous values of changed fields */\n  previousValues: Partial

<Entity>

;\n}\n\n/

 Name of the deleted entity 

 The entity that was deleted (snapshot before deletion) */\n  entity: Entity;\n}"

 

},

 The newly created relation */\n  relation: Relation;\n}\n\n/

/\n  relationCount: number;\n  /

* Bytes written to disk (if available) */\n  bytesWritten?: number;\n}"

 

},

"code": "/

\n * Map of event types to their payload types.\n * Used for type-safe event handling.\n */\nexport interface GraphEventMap {\n  entityCreated: EntityCreatedEvent;\n  entityUpdated: EntityUpdatedEvent;\n  entityDeleted: EntityDeletedEvent;\n  relationCreated: RelationCreatedEvent;\n  relationDeleted: RelationDeletedEvent;\n  observationAdded: ObservationAddedEvent;\n  observationDeleted: ObservationDeletedEvent;\n  graphLoaded: GraphLoadedEvent;\n  graphSaved: GraphSavedEvent;\n}\n\n/

\n * Type-safe event listener function.\n */\nexport type GraphEventListener

<T extends GraphEventType>

 = (\n  event: GraphEventMap[T]\n) => void;"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 9,

 

"action": "Add GraphEventEmitter class",

 

"code": "/

\n * Type-safe EventEmitter for graph changes.\n *\n * Wraps Node.js EventEmitter to provide type safety for event names\n * and payloads. Automatically adds timestamps to all emitted events.\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * const emitter = new GraphEventEmitter();\n *\n * // Subscribe to entity creation\n * emitter.on('entityCreated', (event) => {\n *   console.log(`New entity: ${event.entity.name} at ${event.timestamp}`);\n * });\n *\n * // Subscribe to updates with change tracking\n * emitter.on('entityUpdated', (event) => {\n *   console.log(`Updated: ${event.entity.name}`);\n *   console.log('Changes:', event.changes);\n *   console.log('Previous:', event.previousValues);\n * });\n *\n * // One-time listener\n * emitter.once('graphLoaded', (event) => {\n *   console.log(`Loaded ${event.entityCount} entities`);\n * });\n * 

\n */\nexport class GraphEventEmitter {\n  private emitter = new EventEmitter();\n\n  /

\n   * Set maximum listeners per event type.\n   * @param n - Maximum number of listeners (default: 10)\n   */\n  setMaxListeners(n: number): this {\n    this.emitter.setMaxListeners(n);\n    return this;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Register a listener for a graph event.\n   * @param event - Event type to listen for\n   * @param listener - Callback function\n   */\n  on

(\n    event: T,\n    listener: GraphEventListener

\n  ): this {\n    this.emitter.on(event, listener);\n    return this;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Register a one-time listener for a graph event.\n   * The listener is automatically removed after first invocation.\n   * @param event - Event type to listen for\n   * @param listener - Callback function\n   */\n  once

<T extends GraphEventType>

(\n    event: T,\n    listener: GraphEventListener

<T>

\n  ): this {\n    this.emitter.once(event, listener);\n    return this;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Remove a listener for a graph event.\n   * @param event - Event type\n   * @param listener - Callback function to remove\n   */\n  off

(\n    event: T,\n    listener: GraphEventListener

\n  ): this {\n    this.emitter.off(event, listener);\n    return this;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Remove all listeners for a specific event or all events.\n   * @param event - Optional event type (removes all if not specified)\n   */\n  removeAllListeners(event?: GraphEventType): this {\n    this.emitter.removeAllListeners(event);\n    return this;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Emit a graph event.\n   * Automatically adds timestamp to the payload.\n   *\n   * @internal Used by GraphStorage to emit events on mutations.\n   * @param event - Event type\n   * @param payload - Event payload (without timestamp)\n   * @returns True if event had listeners\n   */\n  emit

(\n    event: T,\n    payload: Omit<GraphEventMap[T], 'timestamp'>\n  ): boolean {\n    const fullPayload = {\n      ...payload,\n      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n    };\n    return this.emitter.emit(event, fullPayload);\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get the number of listeners for an event.\n   * @param event - Event type\n   */\n  listenerCount(event: GraphEventType): number {\n    return this.emitter.listenerCount(event);\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get all registered event names.\n   */\n  eventNames(): GraphEventType[] {\n    return this.emitter.eventNames() as GraphEventType[];\n  }\n}"

},

\n   * Set of terms that need IDF recalculation.\n   * Deferred recalc avoids overhead on frequent updates.\n   */\n  private dirtyTerms: Set

 = new Set();\n\n  /

\n   * Total document count for IDF calculation.\n   * Cached to avoid recounting on every update.\n   */\n  private documentCount: number = 0;"

{

 

"step": 3,

 

"action": "Add addEntity method after updateIndex() method (around line 163)",

 

"code": "  /

\n   * Add a single entity to the index incrementally.\n   *\n   * O(log n) operation - only updates the document vector for the new entity\n   * and marks affected terms as dirty for lazy IDF recalculation.\n   *\n   * @param entity - Entity to add to the index\n   * @returns True if added, false if entity already indexed\n   */\n  addEntity(entity: Entity): boolean {\n    if (!this.index) {\n      // No index exists - caller should build first\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    if (this.index.documents.has(entity.name)) {\n      // Already indexed\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    // Build document text and tokenize\n    const documentText = [\n      entity.name,\n      entity.entityType,\n      ...entity.observations,\n    ].join(' ');\n\n    const tokens = tokenize(documentText);\n    const tokenSet = new Set(tokens);\n\n    // Calculate term frequencies\n    const termFreq: Record<string, number> = {};\n    for (const term of tokens) {\n      termFreq[term] = (termFreq[term] || 0) + 1;\n      // Mark term as dirty for IDF recalc\n      this.dirtyTerms.add(term);\n    }\n\n    // Add document vector\n    this.index.documents.set(entity.name, {\n      entityName: entity.name,\n      terms: termFreq,\n      documentText,\n    });\n\n    this.documentCount++;\n    this.index.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();\n\n    return true;\n  }"

},

{

"step": 4,

"action": "Add removeEntity method after addEntity()",

"code": "  /

\n   * Remove a single entity from the index incrementally.\n   *\n   * O(log n) operation - removes the document vector and marks affected\n   * terms as dirty for lazy IDF recalculation.\n   *\n   * @param entityName - Name of entity to remove\n   * @returns True if removed, false if entity not in index\n   */\n  removeEntity(entityName: string): boolean {\n    if (!this.index) {\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    const doc = this.index.documents.get(entityName);\n    if (!doc) {\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    // Mark all terms from this document as dirty\n    for (const term of Object.keys(doc.terms)) {\n      this.dirtyTerms.add(term);\n    }\n\n    // Remove document vector\n    this.index.documents.delete(entityName);\n    this.documentCount--;\n    this.index.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();\n\n    return true;\n  }"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 5,

 

"action": "Add updateEntityInIndex method after removeEntity()",

 

"code": "  /

\n   * Update a single entity in the index incrementally.\n   *\n   * Combines remove + add for atomic update. If entity doesn't exist,\n   * performs add only.\n   *\n   * @param entity - Entity with updated data\n   * @returns True if index was modified\n   */\n  updateEntityInIndex(entity: Entity): boolean {\n    if (!this.index) {\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    // Remove old version (if exists) then add new\n    this.removeEntity(entity.name);\n    return this.addEntity(entity);\n  }"

},

{

"step": 6,

"action": "Add recalculateDirtyIDF method after updateEntityInIndex()",

"code": "  /

\n   * Recalculate IDF values for dirty terms.\n   *\n   * Called lazily before search operations to ensure IDF values are accurate.\n   * Uses the existing document vectors to count term occurrences.\n   *\n   * @returns Number of terms recalculated\n   */\n  recalculateDirtyIDF(): number {\n    if (!this.index || this.dirtyTerms.size === 0) {\n      return 0;\n    }\n\n    const totalDocs = this.index.documents.size;\n    if (totalDocs === 0) {\n      // Clear IDF if no documents\n      this.index.idf.clear();\n      this.dirtyTerms.clear();\n      return 0;\n    }\n\n    let recalculated = 0;\n\n    for (const term of this.dirtyTerms) {\n      // Count documents containing this term\n      let docFreq = 0;\n      for (const doc of this.index.documents.values()) {\n        if (term in doc.terms) {\n          docFreq++;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (docFreq === 0) {\n        // Term no longer in any document, remove from IDF\n        this.index.idf.delete(term);\n      } else {\n        // Recalculate IDF: log(totalDocs / docFreq)\n        const idfValue = Math.log(totalDocs / docFreq);\n        this.index.idf.set(term, idfValue);\n      }\n      recalculated++;\n    }\n\n    this.dirtyTerms.clear();\n    this.index.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();\n\n    return recalculated;\n  }"

 

},

\n   * Get count of dirty terms pending recalculation.\n   */\n  getDirtyTermCount(): number {\n    return this.dirtyTerms.size;\n  }"

"step": 5,

"code": "  /**\n   * Subscribe to graph events for incremental index updates.\n   * @private\n   */\n  private subscribeToEvents(events: GraphEventEmitter): void {\n    // Handle entity creation\n    events.on('entityCreated', (event: EntityCreatedEvent) => {\n      if (this.indexManager?.getIndex()) {\n        this.indexManager.addEntity(event.entity);\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Handle entity update\n    events.on('entityUpdated', (event: EntityUpdatedEvent) => {\n      if (this.indexManager?.getIndex()) {\n        this.indexManager.updateEntityInIndex(event.entity);\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Handle entity deletion\n    events.on('entityDeleted', (event: EntityDeletedEvent) => {\n      if (this.indexManager?.getIndex()) {\n        this.indexManager.removeEntity(event.entityName);\n      }\n    });\n  }"

 

},

"code": "/

\n * Estimates query execution cost based on query characteristics and graph state.\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * const estimator = new QueryCostEstimator();\n * const stats = await storage.getGraphStats();\n *\n * // Estimate cost for a search\n * const cost = estimator.estimateSearch('machine learning', 'ranked', stats);\n * console.log(`Estimated time: ${cost.estimatedMs}ms`);\n * console.log(`Complexity: ${cost.complexity}`);\n * console.log(`Recommended: ${cost.recommendedAlgorithm}`);\n *\n * // Analyze a query\n * const analysis = estimator.analyzeQuery('name:Alice AND type:person');\n * console.log(`Terms: ${analysis.termCount}`);\n * console.log(`Uses boolean: ${analysis.hasBooleanOperators}`);\n * 

\n */\nexport class QueryCostEstimator {\n  /

\n   * Estimate the cost of a search operation.\n   *\n   * @param query - The search query string\n   * @param algorithm - The search algorithm to use\n   * @param stats - Current graph statistics\n   * @returns Cost estimate with metrics and recommendations\n   */\n  estimateSearch(\n    query: string,\n    algorithm: SearchAlgorithm,\n    stats: GraphStats\n  ): CostEstimate {\n    const analysis = this.analyzeQuery(query);\n    const entityCount = stats.totalEntities;\n\n    let entityIterations = entityCount;\n    let indexLookups = 0;\n    let usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.BASIC_MATCH_US_PER_ENTITY;\n    let canUseIndex = false;\n\n    // Adjust based on algorithm\n    switch (algorithm) {\n      case 'basic':\n        usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.BASIC_MATCH_US_PER_ENTITY;\n        // Can use name/type index for field-specific queries\n        if (analysis.hasFieldSpecifiers && analysis.targetFields.length === 1) {\n          const field = analysis.targetFields[0];\n          if (field === 'name' || field === 'type') {\n            canUseIndex = true;\n            indexLookups = 1;\n            entityIterations = Math.ceil(entityCount * 0.1); // Estimate 10% match\n          }\n        }\n        break;\n\n      case 'ranked':\n        usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.TFIDF_SCORE_US_PER_ENTITY;\n        // Always iterates all entities for scoring\n        break;\n\n      case 'boolean':\n        usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.BASIC_MATCH_US_PER_ENTITY * 1.5;\n        // Uses observation index for term lookups\n        if (!analysis.hasBooleanOperators) {\n          canUseIndex = true;\n          indexLookups = analysis.termCount;\n          entityIterations = Math.ceil(entityCount * 0.2);\n        }\n        break;\n\n      case 'fuzzy':\n        usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.FUZZY_MATCH_US_PER_ENTITY;\n        // Always iterates all entities (no index)\n        break;\n\n      case 'semantic':\n        usPerEntity = COST_CONSTANTS.SEMANTIC_COMPARE_US_PER_ENTITY;\n        // Vector comparison is fast but requires embedding lookup\n        indexLookups = 1; // Embedding generation\n        break;\n    }\n\n    // Calculate estimated time\n    const estimatedMs =\n      (entityIterations * usPerEntity) / 1000 +\n      (indexLookups * COST_CONSTANTS.INDEX_LOOKUP_US) / 1000;\n\n    // Determine complexity\n    let complexity: CostEstimate['complexity'];\n    if (entityIterations < COST_CONSTANTS.LOW_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD) {\n      complexity = 'low';\n    } else if (entityIterations < COST_CONSTANTS.MEDIUM_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD) {\n      complexity = 'medium';\n    } else if (entityIterations < COST_CONSTANTS.HIGH_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD) {\n      complexity = 'high';\n    } else {\n      complexity = 'very_high';\n    }\n\n    // Determine recommended algorithm\n    const recommendedAlgorithm = this.recommendAlgorithm(analysis, stats);\n\n    // Calculate confidence (lower for larger graphs, complex queries)\n    let confidence = 0.8;\n    if (entityCount > 10000) confidence -= 0.1;\n    if (analysis.hasBooleanOperators) confidence -= 0.1;\n    if (algorithm === 'fuzzy') confidence -= 0.1;\n    confidence = Math.max(0.5, confidence);\n\n    // Generate explanation\n    const explanation = this.generateExplanation(\n      algorithm,\n      entityIterations,\n      indexLookups,\n      canUseIndex,\n      estimatedMs\n    );\n\n    return {\n      entityIterations,\n      indexLookups,\n      estimatedMs: Math.round(estimatedMs * 100) / 100,\n      complexity,\n      confidence,\n      canUseIndex,\n      recommendedAlgorithm,\n      explanation,\n    };\n  }"

 

},

"action": "Add analyzeQuery method",

 

"code": "  /**\n   * Analyze a query string to determine its characteristics.\n   *\n   * @param query - The search query string\n   * @returns Analysis of query characteristics\n   

/\n  analyzeQuery(query: string): QueryAnalysis {\n    const normalized = query.toLowerCase().trim();\n\n    // Check for field specifiers (name:, type:, observation:)\n    const fieldPattern = /\b(name|type|observation|entitytype|obs):/gi;\n    const fieldMatches = normalized.match(fieldPattern) || [];\n    const hasFieldSpecifiers = fieldMatches.length > 0;\n\n    // Extract target fields\n    const targetFields = [...new Set(\n      fieldMatches.map(m => m.replace(':', '').toLowerCase())\n    )];\n\n    // Check for boolean operators\n    const hasBooleanOperators =\n      /\b(AND|OR|NOT)\b/i.test(query) ||\n      /[()]/g.test(query);\n\n    // Count terms (excluding operators and field specifiers)\n    const cleanQuery = normalized\n      .replace(fieldPattern, '')\n      .replace(/\b(and|or|not)\b/gi, '')\n      .replace(/[()]/g, '')\n      .trim();\n    const terms = cleanQuery.split(/\s+/).filter(t => t.length > 0);\n    const termCount = terms.length;\n\n    // Determine if fuzzy matching might be needed\n    const requiresFuzzy = /~\d

/.test(query) || /\\*|\\?/.test(query);\n\n    // Determine if ranking would benefit the query\n    const benefitsFromRanking = termCount > 1 && !hasFieldSpecifiers;\n\n    return {\n      termCount,\n      hasFieldSpecifiers,\n      hasBooleanOperators,\n      requiresFuzzy,\n      benefitsFromRanking,\n      targetFields,\n    };\n  }"
},
{
"step": 9,
"action": "Add recommendAlgorithm method",
"code": "  /**\n   * Recommend the optimal search algorithm based on query and graph.\n   *\n   * @param analysis - Query analysis\n   * @param stats - Graph statistics\n   * @returns Recommended search algorithm\n   */\n  recommendAlgorithm(analysis: QueryAnalysis, stats: GraphStats): SearchAlgorithm {\n    // Fuzzy required for wildcard/similarity queries\n    if (analysis.requiresFuzzy) {\n      return 'fuzzy';\n    }\n\n    // Boolean for complex queries with operators\n    if (analysis.hasBooleanOperators) {\n      return 'boolean';\n    }\n\n    // For very large graphs, prefer index-based search\n    if (stats.totalEntities > 10000) {\n      if (analysis.hasFieldSpecifiers) {\n        return 'boolean'; // Uses observation index\n      }\n      return 'basic'; // Simple but fast\n    }\n\n    // For multi-term queries, ranking is valuable\n    if (analysis.benefitsFromRanking && stats.totalEntities > 100) {\n      return 'ranked';\n    }\n\n    // Default to basic for simple queries\n    return 'basic';\n  }"
},

{algorithm} search

);\n\n    if (canUseIndex) {\n      parts.push(

uses index (

{indexLookups} lookup

{indexLookups > 1 ? 's' : ''})

);\n      parts.push(

${entityIterations} entities to scan

);\n    } else {\n      parts.push(

full scan of 

{entityIterations} entities`);\n    }\n\n    parts.push(`~

{estimatedMs.toFixed(1)}ms estimated

);\n\n    return parts.join(', ');\n  }\n}" }, { "step": 11, "action": "Run TypeScript compilation", "details": "Run: npm run typecheck" } ], "acceptanceCriteria": [ "QueryCostEstimator.ts file created in src/search/", "CostEstimate interface with all fields defined", "QueryAnalysis interface with all fields defined", "estimateSearch() returns accurate cost estimates for all algorithms", "analyzeQuery() correctly identifies query characteristics", "recommendAlgorithm() suggests optimal algorithm", "Cost constants are realistic (calibrated to benchmarks)", "Human-readable explanation generated", "Class has comprehensive JSDoc with examples", "npm run typecheck passes" ] }, { "id": "10.4.2", "category": "integration", "title": "Integrate QueryCostEstimator into SearchManager", "description": "Add getCostEstimate() method to SearchManager that uses QueryCostEstimator to provide cost estimates for any search. Add cost estimator as private property and new public methods." }, "stepByStep": [ { "step": 1, "action": "Open src/search/SearchManager.ts", "details": "Open the SearchManager file" }, { "step": 2, "action": "Add import for QueryCostEstimator", "details": "Find the imports at the top and add:\nimport { QueryCostEstimator, type CostEstimate, type SearchAlgorithm, type QueryAnalysis } from './QueryCostEstimator.js';\nimport type { GraphStats, Entity } from '../types/index.js';  // Add GraphStats and Entity if not already imported" }, { "step": 3, "action": "Add private cost estimator property after existing properties", "details": "Find the private properties section and add:\n  private costEstimator: QueryCostEstimator | null = null;\n  private storage: GraphStorage;  // Add this if not already a private property\n\n  /**\n   * Get cost estimator instance (lazy init).\n   * @private\n   */\n  private getCostEstimator(): QueryCostEstimator {\n    if (!this.costEstimator) {\n      this.costEstimator = new QueryCostEstimator();\n    }\n    return this.costEstimator;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Get basic graph statistics for cost estimation.\n   * Note: SearchManager needs a reference to storage. Either add 'private storage: GraphStorage' as a property and store from constructor, or inject these stats differently.\n   * @private\n   */\n  private async getGraphStats(): Promise<GraphStats> {\n    const graph = await this.storage.loadGraph();\n    const entityTypesCounts: Record<string, number> = {};\n    const relationTypesCounts: Record<string, number> = {};\n    \n    for (const entity of graph.entities) {\n      entityTypesCounts[entity.entityType] = (entityTypesCounts[entity.entityType] || 0) + 1;\n    }\n    for (const relation of graph.relations) {\n      relationTypesCounts[relation.relationType] = (relationTypesCounts[relation.relationType] || 0) + 1;\n    }\n    \n    return {\n      totalEntities: graph.entities.length,\n      totalRelations: graph.relations.length,\n      entityTypesCounts,\n      relationTypesCounts,\n    };\n  }" }, { "step": 4, "action": "Add getCostEstimate public method", "code": "  /**\n   * Get cost estimate for a search operation.\n   *\n   * Analyzes the query and current graph state to estimate execution cost,\n   * recommend optimal algorithm, and predict execution time.\n   *\n   * @param query - The search query string\n   * @param algorithm - Algorithm to estimate (default: 'basic')\n   * @returns Promise resolving to cost estimate\n   *\n   * @example\n   * ```typescript\n   * const cost = await searchManager.getCostEstimate('machine learning');\n   * console.log(

Used algorithm: ${result.algorithm}

);\n   * console.log(

Found: ${result.entities.length} entities`);\n   * ```\n   */\n  async searchAuto(\n    query: string,\n    options: {\n      tags?: string[];\n      minImportance?: number;\n      maxImportance?: number;\n      entityType?: string;\n      limit?: number;\n    } = {}\n  ): Promise<{\n    entities: Entity[];\n    algorithm: SearchAlgorithm;\n    costEstimate: CostEstimate;\n  }> {\n    const stats = await this.getGraphStats();\n    const analysis = this.getCostEstimator().analyzeQuery(query);\n    const recommended = this.getCostEstimator().recommendAlgorithm(analysis, stats);\n    const costEstimate = this.getCostEstimator().estimateSearch(query, recommended, stats);\n\n    let entities: Entity[];\n\n    switch (recommended) {\n      case 'ranked': {\n        const results = await this.searchNodesRanked(\n          query,\n          options.tags,\n          options.minImportance,\n          options.maxImportance,\n          options.entityType,\n          options.limit\n        );\n        entities = results.map(r => r.entity);\n        break;\n      }\n\n      case 'boolean': {\n        entities = await this.booleanSearch(\n          query,\n          options.tags,\n          options.minImportance,\n          options.maxImportance,\n          options.limit\n        );\n        break;\n      }\n\n      case 'fuzzy': {\n        const results = await this.fuzzySearch(\n          query,\n          0.6, // Default threshold\n          options.tags,\n          options.minImportance,\n          options.maxImportance,\n          options.limit\n        );\n        entities = results.map(r => r.entity);\n        break;\n      }\n\n      case 'basic':\n      default: {\n        entities = await this.searchNodes(\n          query,\n          options.tags,\n algorithm: recommended,\n      costEstimate,\n    };\n  }"

Version

: 1.1.0

Prerequisites

: Phase 10 complete, All tests passing, SemanticSearch and EmbeddingService operational


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Executive Summary

Phase 11 implements the SimpleMem-inspired Three-Layer Hybrid Search architecture and Intelligent Retrieval system from FUTURE_FEATURES.md (Phases 6-9). This transforms memory-mcp from a storage system into an intelligent memory system with query understanding and adaptive retrieval.

Key Features

Three-Layer Hybrid Search

 - Combine semantic, lexical (BM25), and symbolic (metadata) signals

Query Analysis

 - Decompose complex queries into targeted sub-queries

Reflection-Based Retrieval

 - Iteratively refine results until sufficient

Semantic Compression

 - Normalize observations with coreference resolution

Adaptive Query Intelligence

 - Auto-select optimal search strategy

);\n      } else {\n        return { matches: false, score: 0, matchedFilters: [] };\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Parent filter\n    if (filters.parentId !== undefined) {\n      totalFilters++;\n      if (entity.parentId === filters.parentId) {\n        matchedCount++;\n        matchedFilters.push(

parent:${filters.parentId}

);\n      } else {\n        return { matches: false, score: 0, matchedFilters: [] };\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Has observations filter\n    if (filters.hasObservations !== undefined) {\n      totalFilters++;\n      const hasObs = entity.observations.length > 0;\n      if (hasObs === filters.hasObservations) {\n        matchedCount++;\n        matchedFilters.push('hasObservations');\n      } else {\n        return { matches: false, score: 0, matchedFilters: [] };\n      }\n    }\n\n    // If no filters specified, match all with base score\n    if (totalFilters === 0) {\n      return { matches: true, score: 0.5, matchedFilters: [] };\n    }\n\n    // Score based on proportion of filters matched\n    const score = matchedCount / totalFilters;\n    return { matches: true, score, matchedFilters };\n  }"

},

{

"step": 6,

"action": "Add helper methods",

"code": "  /

\n   * Get entities matching a specific tag.\n   */\n  byTag(entities: Entity[], tag: string): Entity[] {\n    return entities.filter(e =>\n      e.tags?.some(t => t.toLowerCase() === tag.toLowerCase())\n    );\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get entities of a specific type.\n   */\n  byType(entities: Entity[], entityType: string): Entity[] {\n    return entities.filter(e =>\n      e.entityType.toLowerCase() === entityType.toLowerCase()\n    );\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Get entities within importance range.\n   */\n  byImportance(entities: Entity[], min: number, max: number): Entity[] {\n    return entities.filter(e => {\n      const imp = e.importance ?? 5;\n      return imp >= min && imp <= max;\n    });\n  }\n}"

 

},

"id": "11.1.3",

 

"category": "search",

 

"title": "Create HybridSearchManager Class",

 

"description": "Create the main hybrid search orchestrator that combines semantic, lexical, and symbolic search layers with configurable weights.",

 

"status": "completed",

"agent": "haiku",

 

"files": ["src/search/HybridSearchManager.ts"],

 

"testCategories": ["unit", "integration"],

 

"implementation": {

 

"purpose": "Orchestrate the three search layers (semantic, lexical, symbolic) and merge their results using weighted scoring. This is the core of the hybrid search system.",

],

 

"existingCodeContext": "SemanticSearch exists in src/search/SemanticSearch.ts, RankedSearch (TF-IDF) exists in src/search/RankedSearch.ts. SymbolicSearch created in task 11.1.2."

 

},

 

"stepByStep": [

 

{

 

"step": 1,

 

"action": "Create new file src/search/HybridSearchManager.ts",

 

"details": "Create the new file in the search directory"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 2,

 

"action": "Add file header and imports",

 

"code": "/

\n * Hybrid Search Manager\n *\n * Phase 11: Orchestrates three-layer hybrid search combining\n * semantic, lexical, and symbolic signals.\n *\n * @module search/HybridSearchManager\n */\n\nimport type {\n  Entity,\n  HybridSearchOptions,\n  HybridSearchResult,\n  ReadonlyKnowledgeGraph,\n} from '../types/index.js';\nimport type { SemanticSearch } from './SemanticSearch.js';\nimport type { RankedSearch } from './RankedSearch.js';\nimport { SymbolicSearch } from './SymbolicSearch.js';\nimport { SEMANTIC_SEARCH_LIMITS } from '../utils/constants.js';"

},

{

"step": 3,

"action": "Add default weights constant",

"code": "/

\n * Default weights for hybrid search layers.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_HYBRID_WEIGHTS = {\n  semantic: 0.5,\n  lexical: 0.3,\n  symbolic: 0.2,\n};"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 4,

 

"action": "Add HybridSearchManager class with constructor",

 

"code": "/

\n * Hybrid Search Manager\n *\n * Combines three search layers:\n * 1. Semantic: Vector similarity via embeddings\n * 2. Lexical: Keyword matching via TF-IDF/BM25\n * 3. Symbolic: Structured metadata filtering\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * const hybrid = new HybridSearchManager(semanticSearch, rankedSearch);\n * const results = await hybrid.search(graph, 'machine learning', {\n *   semanticWeight: 0.5,\n *   lexicalWeight: 0.3,\n *   symbolicWeight: 0.2,\n *   symbolic: { tags: ['ai'] }\n * });\n * 

\n */\nexport class HybridSearchManager {\n  private symbolicSearch: SymbolicSearch;\n\n  constructor(\n    private semanticSearch: SemanticSearch,\n    private rankedSearch: RankedSearch\n  ) {\n    this.symbolicSearch = new SymbolicSearch();\n  }"

},

{

"step": 5,

"action": "Add main search method",

"code": "  /

\n   * Perform hybrid search combining all three layers.\n   *\n   * @param graph - Knowledge graph to search\n   * @param query - Search query text\n   * @param options - Hybrid search options with weights\n   * @returns Combined and ranked results\n   */\n  async search(\n    graph: ReadonlyKnowledgeGraph,\n    query: string,\n    options: Partial

<HybridSearchOptions>

 = {}\n  ): Promise<HybridSearchResult[]> {\n    const {\n      semanticWeight = DEFAULT_HYBRID_WEIGHTS.semantic,\n      lexicalWeight = DEFAULT_HYBRID_WEIGHTS.lexical,\n      symbolicWeight = DEFAULT_HYBRID_WEIGHTS.symbolic,\n      semantic = {},\n      lexical = {},\n      symbolic = {},\n      limit = SEMANTIC_SEARCH_LIMITS.DEFAULT_LIMIT,\n    } = options;\n\n    // Normalize weights\n    const totalWeight = semanticWeight + lexicalWeight + symbolicWeight;\n    const normSemantic = semanticWeight / totalWeight;\n    const normLexical = lexicalWeight / totalWeight;\n    const normSymbolic = symbolicWeight / totalWeight;\n\n    // Execute searches in parallel\n    const [semanticResults, lexicalResults, symbolicResults] = await Promise.all([\n      this.executeSemanticSearch(graph, query, semantic, limit * 2),\n      this.executeLexicalSearch(graph, query, lexical, limit * 2),\n      this.executeSymbolicSearch(graph.entities, symbolic),\n    ]);\n\n    // Merge results\n    const merged = this.mergeResults(\n      semanticResults,\n      lexicalResults,\n      symbolicResults,\n      { semantic: normSemantic, lexical: normLexical, symbolic: normSymbolic }\n    );\n\n    // Sort by combined score and limit\n    return merged\n      .sort((a, b) => b.scores.combined - a.scores.combined)\n      .slice(0, limit);\n  }"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 6,

 

"action": "Add private layer execution methods",

 

"code": "  /

\n   * Execute semantic search layer.\n   */\n  private async executeSemanticSearch(\n    graph: ReadonlyKnowledgeGraph,\n    query: string,\n    options: { minSimilarity?: number; topK?: number },\n    limit: number\n  ): Promise<Map<string, number>> {\n    const results = new Map<string, number>();\n\n    try {\n      const semanticResults = await this.semanticSearch.search(\n        graph,\n        query,\n        options.topK ?? limit,\n        options.minSimilarity ?? 0\n      );\n\n      for (const result of semanticResults) {\n        results.set(result.entity.name, result.similarity);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      // Semantic search may fail if not indexed\n    }\n\n    return results;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Execute lexical search layer (TF-IDF/BM25).\n   */\n  private async executeLexicalSearch(\n    graph: ReadonlyKnowledgeGraph,\n    query: string,\n    _options: { useStopwords?: boolean; useStemming?: boolean },\n    limit: number\n  ): Promise<Map<string, number>> {\n    const results = new Map<string, number>();\n\n    try {\n      const lexicalResults = await this.rankedSearch.search(graph, query, limit);\n\n      // Normalize scores to 0-1 range\n      const maxScore = Math.max(...lexicalResults.map(r => r.score), 1);\n      for (const result of lexicalResults) {\n        results.set(result.entity.name, result.score / maxScore);\n      }\n    } catch {\n      // Lexical search may fail\n    }\n\n    return results;\n  }\n\n  /

\n   * Execute symbolic search layer.\n   */\n  private executeSymbolicSearch(\n    entities: Entity[],\n    filters: HybridSearchOptions['symbolic']\n  ): Map<string, number> {\n    const results = new Map<string, number>();\n\n    if (!filters || Object.keys(filters).length === 0) {\n      // No symbolic filters, give all entities base score\n      for (const entity of entities) {\n        results.set(entity.name, 0.5);\n      }\n      return results;\n    }\n\n    const symbolicResults = this.symbolicSearch.search(entities, filters);\n    for (const result of symbolicResults) {\n      results.set(result.entity.name, result.score);\n    }\n\n    return results;\n  }"

},

{

"step": 7,

"action": "Add mergeResults method",

"code": "  /

\n   * Merge results from all three layers.\n   */\n  private mergeResults(\n    semanticScores: Map<string, number>,\n    lexicalScores: Map<string, number>,\n    symbolicScores: Map<string, number>,\n    weights: { semantic: number; lexical: number; symbolic: number }\n  ): HybridSearchResult[] {\n    // Collect all unique entity names\n    const allNames = new Set([\n      ...semanticScores.keys(),\n      ...lexicalScores.keys(),\n      ...symbolicScores.keys(),\n    ]);\n\n    const results: HybridSearchResult[] = [];\n\n    for (const name of allNames) {\n      const semantic = semanticScores.get(name) ?? 0;\n      const lexical = lexicalScores.get(name) ?? 0;\n      const symbolic = symbolicScores.get(name) ?? 0;\n\n      const combined =\n        semantic * weights.semantic +\n        lexical * weights.lexical +\n        symbolic * weights.symbolic;\n\n      const matchedLayers: ('semantic' | 'lexical' | 'symbolic')[] = [];\n      if (semantic > 0) matchedLayers.push('semantic');\n      if (lexical > 0) matchedLayers.push('lexical');\n      if (symbolic > 0) matchedLayers.push('symbolic');\n\n      // Skip if no layers matched\n      if (matchedLayers.length === 0) continue;\n\n      results.push({\n        entity: { name, entityType: '', observations: [] } as Entity,\n        scores: { semantic, lexical, symbolic, combined },\n        matchedLayers,\n      });\n    }\n\n    return results;\n  }"

 

},

 

{

 

"step": 8,

 

"action": "Add searchWithEntities method for full entity resolution",

 

"code": "  /**\n   * Search with full entity resolution.\n   */\n  async searchWithEntities(\n    graph: ReadonlyKnowledgeGraph,\n    query: string,\n    options: Partial

<HybridSearchOptions>

 = {}\n  ): Promise<HybridSearchResult[]> {\n    const results = await this.search(graph, query, options);\n\n    // Resolve entity objects\n    const entityMap = new Map(graph.entities.map(e => [e.name, e]));\n\n    return results\n      .map(r => ({\n        ...r,\n        entity: entityMap.get(r.entity.name) ?? r.entity,\n      }))\n      .filter(r => entityMap.has(r.entity.name));\n  }\n}"

 

},

"action": "Run TypeScript compilation",

 

"details": "Run: npm run typecheck"

 

}

\n * Query Analyzer\n *\n * Phase 11: Extracts structured information from natural language queries\n * to enable intelligent search planning.\n *\n * @module search/QueryAnalyzer\n */\n\nimport type { QueryAnalysis, ExtractedEntity, TemporalRange } from '../types/index.js';"

{

"step": 3,

"action": "Add QueryAnalyzer class with analyzeBasic method",

"code": "/

\n * Query Analyzer extracts structured information from queries.\n *\n * Uses rule-based heuristics for reliable extraction of:\n * - Person names\n * - Location names\n * - Organization names\n * - Temporal references\n * - Question type\n * - Query complexity\n *\n * @example\n * 

typescript\n * const analyzer = new QueryAnalyzer();\n * const analysis = analyzer.analyze(\n *   'What projects did Alice work on last month?'\n * );\n * // { query: '...', entities: [...], persons: ['Alice'], temporalRange: { relative: 'last month' }, ... }\n * 

\n */\nexport class QueryAnalyzer {\n  private personIndicators = ['Mr.', 'Mrs.', 'Ms.', 'Dr.', 'Prof.'];\n  private temporalKeywords = [\n    'yesterday', 'today', 'tomorrow',\n    'last week', 'last month', 'last year',\n    'this week', 'this month', 'this year',\n    'next week', 'next month', 'next year',\n  ];\n  private questionKeywords = {\n    factual: ['what', 'who', 'where', 'which'],\n    temporal: ['when', 'how long', 'since', 'until'],\n    comparative: ['compare', 'difference', 'vs', 'versus', 'better', 'worse'],\n    aggregation: ['how many', 'count', 'total', 'sum', 'average'],\n    'multi-hop': ['and then', 'which means', 'therefore', 'related to'],\n    conceptual: ['explain', 'why', 'how does', 'what is the meaning', 'understand'],\n  };\n\n  /

\n   * Analyze a query using rule-based heuristics.\n   * Main entry point - returns full QueryAnalysis.\n   */\n  analyze(query: string): QueryAnalysis {\n    const lowerQuery = query.toLowerCase();\n    const persons = this.extractPersons(query);\n    const locations = this.extractLocations(query);\n    const organizations = this.extractOrganizations(query);\n    const questionType = this.detectQuestionType(lowerQuery);\n    const complexity = this.estimateComplexity(query);\n    \n    // Build entities array from extracted names\n    const entities: ExtractedEntity[] = [\n      ...persons.map(name => ({ name, type: 'person' as const })),\n      ...locations.map(name => ({ name, type: 'location' as const })),\n      ...organizations.map(name => ({ name, type: 'organization' as const })),\n    ];\n    \n    // Calculate confidence based on extraction quality\n    const confidence = this.calculateConfidence(entities, complexity, questionType);\n    \n    return {\n      query,\n      entities,\n      persons,\n      locations,\n      organizations,\n      temporalRange: this.extractTemporalRange(query),\n      questionType,\n      complexity,\n      confidence,\n      requiredInfoTypes: this.detectRequiredInfoTypes(lowerQuery),\n      subQueries: this.decomposeQuery(query),\n    };\n  }\n  \n  /

\n   * Calculate confidence score for the analysis.\n   */\n  private calculateConfidence(\n    entities: ExtractedEntity[],\n    complexity: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high',\n    questionType: QueryAnalysis['questionType']\n  ): number {\n    let confidence = 0.5;\n    \n    // Higher confidence for simple queries\n    if (complexity === 'low') confidence += 0.3;\n    else if (complexity === 'medium') confidence += 0.1;\n    \n    // Higher confidence when entities are detected\n    if (entities.length > 0) confidence += 0.1;\n    \n    // Lower confidence for conceptual queries (harder to satisfy)\n    if (questionType === 'conceptual') confidence -= 0.2;\n    \n    return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, confidence));\n  }"

 

},
